extracted.intended_audience: Goodreads readers and community reviewers (people rating books/stories on Goodreads or crowd-sourced platforms)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for assigning reader ratings and writing short reviews of books/stories using Goodreads' 5-star system and common community dimensions (plot, characters, writing, etc.). Useful for readers, reviewers, and crowd-sourced story raters.

rubrics_metrics.name: The 5-Star Scale (Official)
rubrics_metrics.description: Five-point scale where each star corresponds to a short qualitative phrase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5 stars — "It was amazing"; 4 stars — "Really liked it"; 3 stars — "Liked it"; 2 stars — "It was OK"; 1 star — "Did not like it". Use these as a quick summary of overall judgment; community practice often skews toward emotional response when awarding 5 stars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the story's events, pacing, twists, stakes, and resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for a captivating narrative with meaningful stakes and twists; maintain steady pacing with no sagging middle; provide a resolution that earns the reader's investment. Anti-patterns include meandering subplots, unresolved key conflicts, or pacing that loses momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate character distinctiveness, development, motivations, and the protagonist/antagonist dynamic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer distinct personalities, demonstrable growth or transformation across the book, believable motivations, and a compelling protagonist paired with a worthy antagonist. Weaknesses include flat characters, inconsistent motivations, or lack of believable change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge prose quality, voice, descriptiveness, and technical correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prose should be enjoyable to read, descriptive without being purple, and feature a distinctive voice; the text should contain few typos or errors. Overly ornate language or frequent mechanical errors are negative signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: World-building (genre-relevant)
rubrics_metrics.description: For genres that require it, assess the setting's consistency, sensory detail, and originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good world-building is internally consistent, sensorily rich, and original while remaining legible to the reader. Problems include internal contradictions, thin sensory detail, or derivative settings that confuse rather than immerse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure how strongly the work affects the reader and whether that effect endures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Did the book make the reader feel something? Did it stay with them after reading? Consider re-readability as an indicator of lasting emotional resonance. Lack of emotional engagement or forgettability are negative factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal enjoyment
rubrics_metrics.description: A practical, reader-centered judgement: did the reader want to continue and would they recommend it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether you wanted to keep reading, whether you would recommend the book, and whether the book delivered on its promise (blurb/genre expectations). Personal enjoyment often drives individual ratings and can diverge from technical craft assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goodreads rating distribution and interpretation (Goodreads Quirk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Community-level tendencies that affect how to read and assign ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most popular books cluster between 3.5–4.5 stars; ratings reflect both quality and audience match. A 5-star "amazing" rating is often given for emotional connection more than craft mastery. Interpret aggregate scores cautiously—consider audience fit and distribution rather than raw mean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implications for crowd-sourced story ratings (Reddit/other communities)
rubrics_metrics.description: How Goodreads-style ratings translate to crowd-sourced story-rating contexts and what signals to expect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reader ratings typically reflect a mix of emotional resonance, craft, and genre match. Outlier low ratings (e.g., 1-star) often stem from genre/expectation mismatch rather than pure craft failure. Aggregate scores tend to cluster narrowly; meaningful signal often resides in the distribution (variability, skew, outliers) rather than the mean alone.
